title: Module localizing subcategories are closed under directed colimits of modules
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $D(R)$ be its ordinary unbounded module derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal L$ be a full subcategory closed under isomorphisms, integer shifts, distinguished triangles, retracts, and set-indexed coproducts. Let $I$ be a nonempty small partially ordered set such that every pair of elements has an upper bound, and let $(M_i,u_{ij})_{i\le j}$ be a directed system of $R$-modules: $u_{ii}=1$ and $u_{jk}u_{ij}=u_{ik}$. Write $M=\varinjlim_{i\in I}M_i$ for the colimit in $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], characterized by its compatible universal cocone. If $M_i[0]\in\mathcal L$ for every $i$, then $M[0]\in\mathcal L$. All indexing sets and coproducts lie in the fixed universe of the modules. No Noetherian hypothesis and no injectivity of the transition maps are required.

source.place: Tag 00DB (lemma-directed-colimit-exact), exactness of directed module colimits; agent bar-resolution corollary for localizing subcategories, not the verbatim statement of that tag. Its independent proof is supplied in the delivery report.

proof.text: Let $D:I\to\mathrm{CoCh}(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$ send $i$ to $M_i[0]$ and $i\le j$ to $u_{ij}[0]$. Colimits of complexes are computed degreewise, so $(M[0],(q_i[0])_i)$ is a colimit cocone of $D$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian] the module category is abelian, has all small coproducts and colimits, and its filtered colimits are exact; $I$ is a nonempty directed poset, hence a filtered category, so colimits of shape $I$ are exact. Let $B^\bullet$ be the bar total of $D$ [def-sc-preorder-bar-total]. Since every $D(i)$ is concentrated in degree $0$, its degree $-n$ term is $B^{-n}=B_n=\bigoplus_{i_0\leq\cdots\leq i_n}M_{i_0}$ for $n\geq0$ (chains with repeated indices included), and its positive terms vanish. By [lem-sc-preorder-bar-filtered-augmentation] the canonical augmentation $\epsilon:B^\bullet\to M[0]$ of the colimit cocone is a quasi-isomorphism. No monicity of $u_{ij}$ is used.

source.place: CategoryTheory.PreorderBar.augmentation_quasiIso, applied to the single-degree diagram of modules; Stacks Tag 00DB (algebra-lemma-directed-colimit-exact) for exactness of directed module colimits.

proof.text: The module category is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian]. Apply [lem-kun-grothendieck-derived-coproducts] to the family $M_{i_0}[0]$ indexed by all chains of length $n+1$. Its termwise sum is $B_n[0]$, so $B_n[0]\in\mathcal L$ by the hypothesis on every $M_i[0]$ and closure under coproducts. Finite powers of the small set $I$, and their subsets of chains, lie in the stipulated universe.

source.place: Tags 0A5L (lemma-direct-sums), 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), 0949 (lemma-colim-hocolim); agent assembly with the explicit bar augmentation

proof.text: For $n\geq0$ let $F_n$ be the brutal subcomplex of $B^\bullet$ in degrees $[-n,0]$: use $B^r$ and its differential there and zero terms elsewhere. Inductively $Q(F_n)\in\mathcal L$. The base is $F_0=B_0[0]$. For $n\geq1$ there is the degreewise split short exact sequence $0\to F_{n-1}\to F_n\to B_n[n]\to0$; its quotient has the single term $B_n$ in degree $-n$. By [lem-pc-cone-short-exact-quasi-iso], its cone triangle becomes a distinguished triangle with third term $B_n[n]$ after localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Shift closure and the preceding step put this third term in $\mathcal L$, so triangle closure gives the inductive step.

source.place: Tags 0A5L (lemma-direct-sums), 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), 0949 (lemma-colim-hocolim); agent assembly with the explicit bar augmentation

proof.text: The inclusions $F_n\to B^\bullet$ and $F_n\to F_{n+1}$ are degreewise injective and compatible. Each degree $r\leq0$ is already exhausted when $n\geq-r$, and every positive degree is zero. Thus [lem-pc-derived-module-filtration-telescope], applied to these subcomplexes, supplies a coproduct $S$ of the $Q(F_n)$ and a distinguished triangle $S\to S\to Q(B^\bullet)\to S[1]$. The index $\operatorname{ULift}\mathbf N$ remains in the module universe. Both copies of $S$ lie in $\mathcal L$ by coproduct closure, hence $Q(B^\bullet)\in\mathcal L$ by triangle closure.

source.place: Tags 0A5L (lemma-direct-sums), 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), 0949 (lemma-colim-hocolim); agent assembly with the explicit bar augmentation

proof.text: Localization inverts the quasi-isomorphism $\epsilon$ of step 1 [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Therefore $Q(B^\bullet)\cong M[0]$, and closure under isomorphisms gives $M[0]\in\mathcal L$.
